Exactly the tests named in permittedFailures may fail. Any different failure, any new failure,
or any change to these lists is a gate failure. A count-only baseline is insufficient: it stays
green when N different tests fail. This was not hypothetical â€” the second run traded two fixed
failures for one new flake and a count-only view would have read 5 -> 4 as pure improvement.
Verdict-(a)/(c) failures stay RED by design. A red test with a recorded verdict is signal;
converting it to a skip is silence.

skips.mechanism: 18 of the 19 are [SkippableFact] + Skip.IfNot(Mtw00CRedFixturePolicy.RedFixturesEnabled), gated on environment variable MTW00C_RUN_RED == '1'. They are deliberate red fixtures for unimplemented MTW-00C plan-card work, excluded from the default suite so CI stays green. The 19th is CapabilityInvokeCorrelationTraceTests (ticket 096), which shells out to apps/capability-host/node_modules/.bin/vitest and Skip.IfNots when that toolchain is absent â€” it is environment-conditional, so on a machine that has run npm ci in apps/capability-host it RUNS and the suite reports 3204 / 3186 passed / 18 skipped.
skips.notSilent: Mtw00CRedFixtureMetaTests checks both the pending and production states on every run, so the skip set cannot drift unnoticed. This is the good version of a skip: gated, reasoned, and covered by a meta-test â€” unlike a missing fixture that skips a test that should have run.

verdictVocabulary.note: No prose definition of these verdict letters exists anywhere in this repository; they were used in this file and in hull-test-baseline.json without a key. Recorded here so the next reader is not guessing.
verdictVocabulary.a-pre-existing-at-sha: Fails at the pinned source sha too. Not caused by the migration.
verdictVocabulary.c-destination-identity-coupled: Fails because the destination tree deliberately does not carry something the source did.
verdictVocabulary.d-host-platform-coupled: Passes on one host OS and fails on another with source byte-identical. Introduced by the winhub relocation from macOS to native Windows. NO CURRENT MEMBERS: both entries in this class have been fixed at source - the carrier separator in harborline-api e2803cf, and the HKDF derivation in 3ac96df. The definition is kept because the class is real and will recur on the next host move.
verdictVocabulary.e-gate-ordering-coupled: Passes in a developer working tree and fails only in the exact-clone gate, because of the order in which the gate performs its steps. NO CURRENT MEMBERS: the single entry in this class was fixed by correcting the gate rather than by carrying it as debt. Kept as a definition because the class is a real hazard whenever a gate step depends on a later step.

flakeRegistry.identity: `test` is the identity the runner prints on its Failed line: the fully qualified name for a plain test, the DisplayName string when the test declares one (`method` then records the method, for the reader).
flakeRegistry.rules: Every row is exact, owned by a ticket, dated (firstSeen) and expiring. An expired or unowned row fails the gate. Validated by eng/flake-registry.mjs; ratcheted by REGISTERED_FLAKE_COUNT there, which must move in the same commit as any growth.
flakeRegistry.retry: ONE identical retry per registered row; both outcomes are recorded in the exact-clone report's host-flake-retry step.
